Greece.Take a look at the pictures.What does ancient Greece make you think of?Ancient Greece is famous for its buildings, especially the temples.Built in the 5th century BC, the Parthenon temple is considered one of the most famous cultural landmarks in Greece.The well-known figure in the bathtub is Archimedes, one of the greatest scientists and mathematicians in history.In fact, ancient Greece is famous for its great talent, such as the thinkers, writers and scientists.We are all familiar with modern Olympic games.But do you know the first ancient Olympic games were held in Greece about 2800 years ago?Actually, the first modern Olympic games were also held in Greece in 1896.The last picture shows us a famous legend, Paris and the Golden Apple.A legend is a story from ancient times about people and events that may or may not be true.Greek legends are valuable treasures of the world.This unit allows us to go into several Greek legends that you may find fun to read.The story we read today, The Knight of the Horse, is part of the legend of the Trojan War.If you haven't read or heard of the story before, you can raise questions that you have interest in.You can take a closer look at the title and the picture.To me, my attention is totally attracted by the huge horse.So I wonder, who built the horse?And why they built the horse?It's okay that you may raise different Greeks built the horse.The Greeks here refers to the soldiers from Greece.From line 6 to line 8, the soldiers built the horse.The Greek here refers to the soldiers from Greece.From line 6 to line 8, we can learn that the Greeks left the horse behind.So it was the Greeks who built the horse.Why did the Greeks build the horse?At the end of the story, the writer tells us the Greeks captured the city through a trick.Here, the city refers to the city of Troy.So the Greeks built the horse to trick the children.The children means the people in Troy.By answering these two questions, we know that the children and the Greeks were at war for 10 years, and the horse helped the Greeks win the war in one night.As the title suggests, the story mainly tells us what happened before, during, and after the night.Read the story again and divide the story into four parts based on the timeline, and summarize the main idea of each part by completing the table on your worksheet.Pay attention to the adverbial phrases of time.Let's go.The first part is from line 1 to line 18.It mainly tells us how the children found the wooden horse and that later they dragged the horse into the city before night.Drag here means pour something along the ground, often with difficulty.The wooden horse was so huge that the children poured it inside with difficulty.The second part is from line 19 to line 24.It mainly tells us how the children celebrated around the horse in the main square.The children celebrated because they thought that the Greeks had left and they had won the war.From line 25 to line 26, the story tells us the square was empty except for the horse by midnight.It means everyone went to sleep before midnight, and at midnight, there was only the horse left in the square.The last part is from line 26 to line 40.It tells us what happened after the six Greek soldiers waited for another hour.They climbed out of the horse and helped the Greek army capture the city of Troy.Capture means take control of.In the end, the Greeks won the war and took control of the city of Troy.When you want to summarize the main idea, you need to pay attention to the characters' actions and try to build the relationship between the characters and some key elements, like the knight and the horse in this story.Now it's time for us to go into details.Read the first part of the story and answer the two questions.How did the captain know the Greeks had gone?What did the horse look like?The first question is, how did the captain know that the Greeks had gone?There are four characteristics within the work.Take a look at the huge wooden horse again and complete the sentences.Why did the horse have to be designed this way?The horse must be large enough for six Greek soldiers.So it was possible for them to stay inside for such a long time.There should be a secret door so that the soldiers could open it and climb out.As a secret door, it should not be easily discovered by the children.The horse had to be on wheels, or the children might fail to put it inside.Failing to move the horse inside could put an end to the trick.What can we learn from the story?Different people may have different ideas.Some may conclude that sometimes intelligence is more important than strength.The Greeks didn't win the war by fighting.They used their intelligence to beat the children.We should never judge people by their looks.The wooden horse was thought of as a gift.But in fact, it was just a ticket to the city.Think twice before acting.The captain never thought of the possibility that the horse could be a trick.On the contrary, the Greeks designed such a careful plan to make the trick work.We should never be too proud.When the children made jokes about the Greeks and called them stupid, it never occurred to them that they were the losers in the end.They paid their price for being too proud to guard the gates.In today's lesson, we have a general understanding of the story.We will
